Alle Parzellen gleichartig, Behandlungen: All plots alike, treatments distributed completely at random.
Wann? Wenn das Versuchsmaterial homogen:
When? When the experimental material is homogeneous (greenhouse, lab, uniform soil).

How? Each treatment is repeated r times, all plots are assigned completely at random.

Input: treatments (number or names) and replications.

The simplest design, but it does not control nuisance effects such as soil gradients.
Feld in Blöcke geteilt, jede Behandlung: Field divided into blocks, each treatment occurs once in every block.
Wann? Wenn es einen Gradienten im Feld g:
When? When there is a gradient in the field (soil, slope, light). Place the blocks across the gradient so that plots within a block are as similar as possible.

How? Each block is a replication and contains all treatments once, in random order.

Input: treatments and number of blocks.
Zwei Störrichtungen: jede Behandlung ste: Two nuisance directions: each treatment occurs once in every row and column.
Wann? Wenn Unterschiede in zwei Richtung:
When? When differences occur in two directions (e.g. slope and direction of cultivation).

How? The field is a square, rows = columns = number of treatments. Each treatment occurs exactly once per row and per column.

Practical up to about 8 to 10 treatments, since the number of plots grows quadratically.
Lateinisches Quadrat mit einem zweiten B: Latin square with a second treatment factor (three nuisance directions).
Wann? Wenn neben Zeilen und Spalten noch:
When? When, besides rows and columns, a third nuisance factor is to be controlled, or two treatment factors with k levels each are tested in a k x k square.

How? Two mutually orthogonal Latin squares are superimposed: each combination of treatment 1 and 2 occurs exactly once, both factors occur once per row and column.

Input: two treatment factors with the same number of levels.

Limits: For order 2 and 6 no such square exists. The app offers odd orders, 4, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24 ... (The agricolae help mentions odd orders as well as 4, 8, 10 and 12.)
Mehrere Faktoren, alle Kombinationen wer: Several factors, all combinations are tested.
Wann? Wenn du zwei oder mehr Faktoren gl:
When? When you want to study two or more factors at the same time and detect interactions (e.g. fertilization x variety).

Input: one factor per line, format  Name: levels  (number or comma-separated names), e.g.  N: 0,50,100

Arrangement: determines the layout of the combinations. CRD = completely random, RCBD = in blocks, LSD = Latin square (number of combinations = side length). Replications apply per combination.
Hauptfaktor auf großen Parzellen, Unterf: Main factor on large plots, subfactor on small plots within them.
Wann? Wenn ein Faktor nur auf großen Flä:
When? When one factor is only practical on large areas (tillage, irrigation) and the second factor can be varied more finely (variety, fertilization).

How? The main plots are arranged either in blocks (rcbd), completely at random (crd) or in a Latin square (lsd, then leave r empty). The subfactor is randomized within them.

Note: The subfactor and the interaction are tested more precisely than the main factor.
Faktor A als Streifen in einer Richtung,: Factor A as strips in one direction, factor B across them.
Wann? Wenn beide Faktoren große Flächen:
When? When both factors need large areas (e.g. sprinkler irrigation in one direction, tillage across it).

How? In each block the levels of A are randomized as rows and the levels of B as columns. The plots are the crossings.

The interaction A x B is tested more precisely, the main effects less precisely.
Mehr Behandlungen als in einen Block pas: More treatments than fit in one block, each pair together equally often.
Wann? Wenn ein Block nur k der t Behandl:
When? When a block can only hold k of the t treatments (e.g. few plants per pot or limited block size).

Property: Each treatment occurs r times, each pair of treatments occurs equally often (λ times) in the same block.

Input: treatments and block size k. Leave r empty to search for the smallest possible number of replications.

Not every combination is possible (condition: r(k-1) = λ(t-1)). On an error the app lists possible r values.
Unvollständiges Lateinisches Quadrat: we: Incomplete Latin square: fewer columns than treatments.
Wann? Wie ein Lateinisches Quadrat (Zeil:
When? Like a Latin square (row and column effect), but when not all treatments fit in one row.

How? There are t rows and r columns (r < t). Each treatment occurs exactly once in every column; the rows form a balanced incomplete block design in which each pair of treatments occurs together equally often.

Input: treatments and number of columns r. Possible only if r(r-1) is divisible by t-1 and a symmetric BIB design exists (e.g. t=7 with r=3 or 4, t=11 with r=5, t=13 with r=4).
Quadratzahl an Behandlungen, Blöcke aus: Square number of treatments, blocks from rows, columns (and diagonals).
When? With many treatments (k x k, e.g. 9, 16, 25 varieties) and small blocks of size k.

How? The treatments are placed in a k x k grid. Simple lattice (r=2): replication 1 = rows, replication 2 = columns as blocks. Triple lattice (r=3): additionally a third replication from the diagonals. Each pair of treatments occurs at most once in the same block.

Input: number of treatments (square number) and type.
Viele Behandlungen, jede Wiederholung in: Many treatments, each replication divided into small blocks.
Wann? Bei vielen Behandlungen, z. B. Sor:
When? With many treatments, e.g. variety trials with 30 to 100 varieties, when large blocks would be too heterogeneous.

How? Each replication contains all treatments once and is divided into small blocks of size k. The blocks are chosen so that pairs of treatments occur together as evenly as possible.

Input: The number of treatments must be a multiple of k, at least 2 replications. Treatments = s x k (s blocks per replication).

Difference to R: There only certain combinations (r = 2 to 4, k <= s) are provided. The app finds the generating array itself and accepts more cases. The figures below the plan show how balanced it is.
Blöcke entstehen durch zyklisches Versch: Blocks are created by cyclically shifting starting blocks.
Wann? Bei 6 bis 30 Behandlungen (laut ag:
When? With 6 to 30 treatments (according to the agricolae help), when only small blocks are possible and an efficient, robust plan is wanted.

How? A starting block with k treatments is shifted cyclically t times and gives t blocks; each starting block provides k replications. With r = i x k, i starting blocks are used.

Input: treatments, block size k and replications r (multiple of k).

Note: The app finds the starting blocks itself (pair frequencies as even as possible).

Row-column arrangement (rowcol = yes): The blocks become rows, the k positions become columns. Each treatment occurs exactly once in every column per starting block, so a column effect (e.g. slope across the rows) is controlled in addition. Each starting block gives a grid of t rows and k columns.
Vergleichssorten in jedem Block, neue Be: Check varieties in every block, new treatments only once.
Wann? Frühe Selektionsstufen mit vielen:
When? Early selection stages with many new breeding lines and little material, when not every new treatment can be replicated.

How? The check varieties (checks) are in every block, the new treatments occur once each and are distributed randomly over the blocks. The checks allow block differences to be estimated. The standard error between checks is much smaller than between two new treatments in different blocks.

Input: checks, new treatments (each number or names) and number of blocks.
Drei Faktoren in drei Stufen: Hauptparze: Three factors on three levels: main plot, subplot, sub-subplot.
Wann? Wenn ein Faktor große Parzellen br:
When? When one factor needs large plots (e.g. irrigation), a second medium ones (e.g. fungicide) and a third small ones (e.g. variety).

How? Per block (rcbd) or per replication (crd) the main plots are arranged randomly, within them the subplots and within those the sub-subplots. The factor on the smallest level is tested most precisely.

Input: levels per tier (number or names), blocks and arrangement.
Resolvierbare unvollständige Blöcke: jed: Resolvable incomplete blocks: each replication contains all treatments.
Wann? Viele Behandlungen, aber nur klein:
When? Many treatments, but only small homogeneous blocks possible.

How? t treatments are distributed over r replications with t/k blocks of size k each. The app swaps treatments between blocks until pairs of treatments occur together in a block as equally often as possible.

Input: treatments (multiple of k), block size k, replications. Check values are shown below the plan (max. pair frequency).
Spezieller resolvierbarer Blockplan für: Special resolvable block design for t = k·(k+1) treatments.
Wann? Wenn die Behandlungszahl ein Produ:
When? When the number of treatments is a product of two consecutive numbers (12, 20, 30, 42, 56 ...) and no square number is available for a square lattice.

How? Like the resolvable IBD, with block size k and k+1 blocks per replication.

Input: treatments (= k·(k+1)), block size k, replications.
Blöcke in zwei Richtungen: Zeilen und Sp: Blocks in two directions: rows and columns per replication.
Wann? Wenn Störeinflüsse sowohl quer als:
When? When nuisance effects occur both across and along the field and there are more treatments than a Latin square sensibly allows.

How? Each replication is a grid of rows and columns (columns = treatments / rows). By swapping, pairs of treatments are distributed as evenly as possible over shared rows and columns.

Input: treatments, rows per replication, replications.
Unwiederholte Linien, Checks auf Diagona: Unreplicated lines, checks on diagonals in the field.
Wann? Frühe Selektion mit vielen Linien:
When? Early selection with many lines and little seed, when only the checks are replicated.

How? The field has a fixed format (rows x columns). The checks are placed systematically on diagonals and form a grid for the spatial analysis; lines are distributed randomly over the remaining plots. The number of check plots results from field size minus lines.

Input: field size, lines, checks, numbering (serpentine = every second row backwards). Decision blocks (several experiments) are not included.
Unwiederholte Linien, Checks möglichst g: Unreplicated lines, checks spread as evenly as possible over rows and columns.
Wann? Wie bei der Diagonal-Anordnung, we:
When? Like the diagonal arrangement, when every row and column should contain at least one check and the checks should be far apart.

How? The check plots are chosen step by step where there are still rows/columns without a check and the distance to existing checks is greatest. Checks with the same name are spread as far apart as possible. Below the plan it says how many rows/columns remain without a check.
Teilweise Wiederholung: manche Genotypen: Partial replication: some genotypes 1x, others 2x, checks more often.
Wann? Wenn Material für Wiederholungen n:
When? When there is only enough material for replications of some of the genotypes.

How? Specify groups of number of genotypes and replications, e.g. 250 genotypes 1x, 85 genotypes 2x, 3 genotypes 8x. Remaining field plots are filled with fillers. The copies of a genotype are spread apart spatially by swapping. The column 'type' shows the number of replications.
Linien auf mehrere Orte verteilen, jede: Spread lines over several locations, each line at only some of the locations.
Wann? Wenn Material oder Fläche nicht er:
When? When material or area do not allow testing every line at every location.

How? Each line is assigned to the given number of locations (smaller than the number of locations), the location sizes are balanced. Checks are at every location. Each location is arranged randomly (column 'block' = location); there are no field rows/columns yet.
